summary: The new module has a real atomicity bug around `prev_action_sha`, plus two verification-path gaps: GET refusal handling is incomplete, and SoD is only enforced on write, not on verification.

findings.message: `append_action()` computes `prev_action_sha` by calling `last_action_sha(ledger)` before it acquires the ledger's write lock. Two concurrent callers can both read the same head, then both append successfully, leaving the second ACTION record pointing at a stale predecessor and making `verify_actions()` fail on a perfectly valid ledger. The same unlocked `ledger.verify()` call can also spuriously raise `TORN` if another writer is in the middle of appending. This needs to be folded into `ledger.append_guarded()` or another atomic read-decide-append path.

`snapshot()` only catches `ActionError`, but `verify_actions()` iterates `ledger.verify()`, which raises `LedgerError` for real refusal cases like `TORN`, `BROKEN_CHAIN`, `FORGED`, or `TRUNCATED`. In those cases `/action_chain` will throw instead of returning the structured `{ok:false, kind:...}` response this function is clearly trying to provide.

The verifier never re-checks the separation-of-duties invariant. `append_action()` rejects duplicate roles on write, but `verify_actions()` accepts any ACTION payload whose hashes chain, even if `creator == reviewer` or similar. That means an ACTION written directly through `ledger.append()` or by another buggy caller will still report as `MEASURED`, which breaks the core guarantee this module advertises.
